<user_message>
Implement the Sticky Asymmetric Columns block layout according to the new schema.

Context:
We are implementing fluid.glass-inspired layouts. We need a new block (or updating an existing one, like `asymmetric-image`) to support a "Sticky Asymmetric Columns" pattern, where one side (usually typography/text) pins via `position: sticky` while the other side (media/cards) scrolls independently.
Reference: `docs/architecture/FLUID-GLASS-BENTO-SCHEMA.md`.

Instructions:
1. Review the "Sticky Asymmetric Columns" section in `docs/architecture/FLUID-GLASS-BENTO-SCHEMA.md`.
2. Create or refactor a block blueprint (e.g., `site/blueprints/blocks/asymmetric-columns.yml` or updating `asymmetric-image.yml`) and its corresponding snippet.
3. Ensure the CSS uses `position: sticky` for the text column and `height: max-content` (or similar) while the opposite column has enough content to allow independent scrolling.
4. Signal completion using the `attempt_completion` tool with a concise summary of the implementation.

These specific instructions supersede any conflicting general instructions. Work ONLY on the Sticky Asymmetric Columns implementation.
</user_message>

File: docs/architecture/FLUID-GLASS-BENTO-SCHEMA.md 1 | # Fluid.glass Bento Grid & Layout Engine Schema 2 | 3 | ## 1. Core Philosophy: The Mathematical Canvas 4 | The "fluid.glass" aesthetic relies on brutalist, high-end structural patterns where the grid acts as a flawless mathematical canvas. To achieve this, our layout engine must enforce **absolute uniformity and extreme gap precision**. Sub-pixel rendering issues or varying margins between components are unacceptable. 5 | 6 | ## 2. Re-engineering the Bento Grid 7 | 8 | ### Current State vs. Target State 9 | Currently, blocks like `bento-grid.php` may rely on ad-hoc flexbox or loose CSS grid implementations that can lead to inconsistent gaps or alignment issues depending on content. The target state is a rigid CSS Grid framework where the grid defines the structure, and items conform to it perfectly. 10 | 11 | ### Blueprint Refactoring (`site/blueprints/blocks/bento-grid.yml`) 12 | - Remove complex layout settings from the blueprint. 13 | - Implement a simple span-based approach (e.g., `col-span-1`, `col-span-2`, `row-span-1`). 14 | - Provide preset layout configurations (e.g., "Hero Split", "Quadrant", "Feature Showcase") rather than allowing arbitrary, hard-to-control dimensions. 15 | 16 | ### PHP Snippet Refactoring (`site/snippets/blocks/bento-grid.php`) 17 | - **Structure:** The outer container must purely be the grid definition. 18 | ```php 19 |
20 | items()->toBlocks() as $item): ?> 21 |

28 | ``` 29 | 30 | ### CSS Architecture 31 | - Use `display: grid`. 32 | - Define a strict `var(--grid-gap)` globally. 33 | - Use `gap: var(--grid-gap)` exclusively. Never use margins for structural spacing within the bento grid. 34 | - Ensure items have `overflow: hidden` and a consistent `border-radius` (e.g., `var(--bento-radius)`). 35 | - Use `aspect-ratio` where appropriate to maintain perfect geometric shapes regardless of viewport size. 36 | 37 | ## 3. Advanced Structural Layouts 38 | 39 | ### Sticky Asymmetric Columns 40 | This layout pattern involves pinning typographical content on one side while media content scrolls independently on the other. 41 | 42 | **DOM Approach:** 43 | ```html 44 |
45 |

Panel 1

Motion Layer: GSAP & Lenis Integration 79 | 80 | To prepare the DOM for advanced scroll-driven animations and smooth scrolling: 81 | 82 | ### Lenis Smooth Scrolling Prep 83 | - **Global Wrapper:** Ensure all content is wrapped in a smooth scroll container. 84 | ```html 85 | 86 |
87 |
88 | 89 |
90 |
91 | 92 | ``` 93 | - **CSS:** Prevent overscroll on body. `body { overscroll-behavior: none; }`. 94 | 95 | ### GSAP ScrollTrigger Prep 96 | - **Data Attributes:** Use semantic data attributes (`data-scroll-section`, `data-animate-up`, `data-parallax`) instead of specific classes for GSAP targeting. This separates styling logic from animation logic. 97 | - **Hardware Acceleration:** Ensure elements targeted for transforms (especially in the horizontal track or parallax elements) have `will-change: transform` applied via a utility class or GSAP's `force3D: true`. 98 | - **Initialization Context:** When initializing GSAP, use `gsap.context()` bounded to the specific block or section to ensure easy cleanup and prevent memory leaks, especially important in SPA or dynamic routing contexts. 99 | 100 | ```javascript 101 | // Example JS Initialization concept 102 | let ctx = gsap.context(() => { 103 | // Horizontal Scroll Logic 104 | const track = document.querySelector('[data-horizontal-track]'); 105 | gsap.to(track, { 106 | xPercent: -100, 107 | x: () => window.innerWidth, 108 | ease: "none", 109 | scrollTrigger: { 110 | trigger: "[data-horizontal-scroll]", 111 | pin: true, 112 | scrub: 1, 113 | end: () => "+=" + document.querySelector('[data-horizontal-track]').offsetWidth 114 | } 115 | }); 116 | }, sectionElement); // Bound to component
